clue.text: Rejected sparkling water before holiday, drinking large brandy

indicators.note: the reversed run swallows the next piece, as a drinker takes it in
rejected things are sent back, so the run of water and holiday is read from the end

parts.note: soda is fizzy water
vac is short for vacation
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone turns down fizzy water before a break and knocks back a big brandy instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the whole water-plus-holiday run backwards, and 'drinking' has that run take in the size letter. Calvados is the apple brandy of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is an apple brandy distilled in Normandy, so it is one specific example of brandy.

clue.text: Pain borne by left winger

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A footballer playing on the left wing suffers an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borne by' means carried within: the letters run across 'left winger'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden short sharp stab of physical discomfort, a kind of pain.

clue.text: Report of economic upturn

definitions.meaning: a report is a loud bang, like a gun going off
a period of rapid growth in business and trade

explanation.definitionFit: Boom names both a deep resounding bang and a period of strong economic growth.

clue.text: Style of music US composer's bound to follow

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: Samuel Barber was an American composer; the 's adds S
to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: A kind of music that an American composer was destined to come after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to follow' reads like 'certain to come next', but bound is HOP and 'to follow' places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a style of close-harmony unaccompanied singing, usually by male quartets.

clue.text: Authors writing about Murdoch, perhaps, in review of book

indicators.note: the writing abbreviation goes around everything else

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: the novelist's name sits inside the turned-round book
to review is to look back, so the word for book is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
Iris Murdoch was a British novelist; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of a Murdoch

explanation.surface: Writers producing a piece about the newspaper owner Murdoch in a book review.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests Rupert the media owner, but it is the novelist Iris. 'review of' turns the book backwards to EMOT, 'in' seats her inside it, and 'about' wraps the writing abbreviation round everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoirists are people who write memoirs, accounts of their own lives, so they are authors.

clue.text: Workers with no heart for playing

indicators.note: the middle pair of letters of the six-letter word is removed

parts.note: gaming is playing games, especially gambling

explanation.surface: Employees who have lost their enthusiasm for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heart' strips MI, the middle two letters, from GAMING.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a team of manual labourers working together, so it can mean workers.

clue.text: Child minder's annual hire charge?

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, yearly
a rental is a fee paid for hiring something

explanation.surface: A yearly fee for hiring, asked about as if for a babysitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child minder' suggests a paid nanny, but here it is a mother or father, and the possessive makes an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent is the person who looks after a child, so belonging to one is parental.

clue.text: Extremely reliable sort to do more office work?

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word are used

parts.note: a sort or kind is a type

explanation.surface: A thoroughly dependable kind of person ready to take on more clerical duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'reliable' but takes its outside letters, R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Keying a document in again is extra keyboard work of the sort done in an office.

clue.text: Fan roared uncontrollably

indicators.note: letters out of control are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A supporter yelled wildly from the stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrollably' signals rearranging the letters of 'roared'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adorer is a devoted admirer, which is what a fan is.

clue.text: African officer in charge, about to appear in early part of day

indicators.note: the two short pieces are placed inside the word for early day

parts.note: morn is a poetic word for morning
OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding or in charge
CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: An African commanding officer shows up around dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear in' seats the officer and 'about' inside the poetic word for morning, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moroccan is a person from Morocco, a country of North Africa, so is an African.

clue.text: Amount to drink that's both good and bad

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A measure of drink that turns out to be helpful and harmful at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill is a small liquid measure, a quarter of a pint, often of spirits.

clue.text: Gauge, say, people entering trendy bar

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: the people go into the combined trendy-plus-bar piece

parts.note: a strut is a supporting bar in a framework
men can mean people, as in all men

explanation.surface: Measure, for example, the crowd coming into a fashionable pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but is a structural member; 'entering' sends the people inside it. 'say' marks the gauge as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge is a measuring device, one example of an instrument.

clue.text: With one double gin, changes colour

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone having one double gin goes a different colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges I with the letters of 'double gin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo blue is a deep violet-blue shade, a colour.

clue.text: Wood cut away from the front

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for cut is taken off

parts.note: a steak is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Timber trimmed back from the front edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a verb on the wood, but it is a noun, a STEAK, whose front S goes 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard durable tropical timber, so a kind of wood.

clue.text: My foreign text translation lacking book with glossary

indicators.note: the translation word goes without its book abbreviation

parts.note: a crib is a literal translation used by students
a key explains the terms or symbols used, like a glossary

explanation.surface: A student's translation of a foreign text that is missing its book and its word list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation. 'lacking' takes B from CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, as in 'My, what a sight!'

clue.text: Senior ladies neglected needy son

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Elderly women have ignored a son who needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' rearranges the letters of 'needy son'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doyennes are the most senior or respected women in a field or group.

clue.text: Previously mentioned a charity supporting limitless woodland

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so comes after
the word for woodland loses its final limit, its last letter

parts.note: a forest is a large area of woodland
aid is help given in charity

explanation.surface: Something already noted: a charity propping up a vast forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' trims FOREST to FORES, and 'supporting' puts AID beneath it in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal legal word meaning stated or named earlier.

clue.text: See a wild creature flee

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, in references
a moose is a large wild deer

explanation.surface: Look, a wild animal makes a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: V is vide, the Latin 'see' used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leave in a hurry, a jokey way of saying run away.

clue.text: Stop ducks eating bread to start with

indicators.note: the endearment takes in the next letter, as if eating it

parts.note: ducks is a British term of endearment, like dear

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Prevent the ducks from eating bread to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' is not birds but the northern English endearment, DEAR; B goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to bar or exclude someone from doing something, so to stop them.

clue.text: Teacher should impose rules, heads demanded

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: Pupils demanded that the teacher lay down the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes the first letters of 'should impose rules'; 'demanded' reads as asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in British schools address a male teacher by the title used for a knight.

clue.text: Fluctuating rate gets steadier, and that's official

indicators.note: a fluctuating thing shifts about, so the letters of the word are moved

parts.note: surer means more steady, as in a surer footing

explanation.surface: A varying exchange rate becomes more stable, and that is the authorised figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluctuating' rearranges RATE as TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is an officer who manages the funds of a club or society, an official.

clue.text: Understanding where pub's to be built, according to report

indicators.note: what is heard when the phrase is said replaces its spelling

parts.note: the plot for a new pub is an inn site

explanation.surface: Insight into where a new pub is to go, as the papers say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to report' means as heard: INN SITE, the location of a pub, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep perception or grasp of something, so understanding.

clue.text: Complaint from groom, losing space for horse

indicators.note: the groom word loses one part, and another takes its place

parts.note: taken as written
room means space
a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat

explanation.surface: A stable hand complains about the lack of space for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing space for horse' swaps ROOM out of GROOM for ROAN, leaving G + ROAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a grumble or protest, so a complaint.

clue.text: Greek island supplying charcuterie

definitions.meaning: an island in the Saronic Gulf, site of a famous ancient sea battle
cured sausages of a kind sold by a delicatessen

explanation.definitionFit: Salamis is an island off Athens; salamis is also the plural of the Italian cured sausage.

clue.text: Troublemaker with yen to capture Italian land

indicators.note: the troublemaker with yen surrounds the Italian, holding it inside

parts.note: a terror is a mischievous person, especially a child
IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A rebel longing to seize an Italian's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' reads as longing but is the currency symbol; 'to capture' has the troublemaker plus that symbol hold the Italian abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Territory is an area of land under a ruler or state.

clue.text: Unremarkable fighter not first to board aircraft

indicators.note: the shortened fighter goes inside the aircraft, as a passenger boards

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

indicators.note: the fighter word loses its first letter

parts.note: a ninja is a Japanese martial-arts warrior

explanation.surface: An ordinary fighter pilot is not first in line to board the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighter' suggests a jet but is a Japanese warrior; 'not first' leaves INJA, and 'to board' puts it inside the aircraft after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain Jane is a woman considered ordinary in looks, so unremarkable.

clue.text: I shall, after getting up, stagger outside and behave boisterously

indicators.note: the stagger word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to rock is to sway or stagger

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: Someone who, after rising, staggers about and makes merry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns the contraction to LLI, read upwards in the down clue; 'outside' has the stagger word wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rollick is to romp or frolic in a high-spirited boisterous way.

clue.text: No 1 for Middlesex put in to get a century?

definitions.text: No 1 for Middlesex put in to get a century?

indicators.note: the initial is placed inside the pair of pieces that follow

parts.note: to cop is to get or catch

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of the word

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, a cricket century

explanation.surface: Is this Middlesex's top batsman, sent in to score a hundred?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: M goes into COP, then TON. Denis Compton was a star batsman for Middlesex, an English county cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Compton was Middlesex's leading batsman of the 1940s, known for scoring hundreds.

clue.text: Part of target victor missed at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the victor word is left out

parts.note: a winner is a victor

explanation.surface: The champion archer misses the bull with the opening shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed at first' drops the W from WINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of an archery or shooting target just outside the bullseye.

clue.text: Thin on the ground, say, ultimately

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the three words before it is used

explanation.surface: Sparse on the ground, so to speak, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of 'the ground, say': E, D, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice or figure is thin and high or slender, like a reed.

clue.text: Left trailer for youngster

parts.note: a trailer is an advertisement for a film, an ad

explanation.surface: A young person left behind a trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' suggests a vehicle but is a film advert, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a boy or young man, a youngster.
